title: Architecture for the recommendation engine
prompt: You're recommending items from a catalog of millions to tens of millions of users. New users and new items arrive constantly, the catalog turns over quickly, and recommendations must render in the page's hot path. Which recommendation architecture do you build?
constraint: Must handle cold-start (new users and new items) and stay fresh, all at low serving latency.

options.why: CF learns only from historical interactions, so it has no signal for brand-new users or items — the textbook cold-start failure the constraint forbids. Embeddings are also retrained in batch, so freshly added items stay invisible until the next training run, violating freshness. It serves fast, but fails two of the three required pillars.

Defensible: item features solve new-item cold-start instantly and similarity lookups are cheap and fresh. But it has no fix for new-user cold-start (no prior engagement to match against) and tends to over-specialize into a filter bubble, so it only partially satisfies the constraint — passable, not best.

Directly satisfies every pillar of the constraint. Candidate generation blends CF with content/embedding retrieval so new items and new users get covered, a streaming feature store keeps signals fresh, and the cheap retrieve-then-rank split keeps the hot path within latency budget by ranking only a few hundred candidates. Best fit.

A rich model can incorporate content features (helping cold-start) and fresh signals, but scoring millions of items on every request blows the latency budget — the exact reason real systems use two-stage retrieval. It optimizes one pillar at the cost of the hard latency constraint, so it's rejected.
